BLUF: The two "hidden" fields are the command-bar Find and Goto inputs — functional, key-bound to / and g, crushed to ghost text by a height: 3 bordered row. Deleting them needs a replacement surface: variant A (summon line) reclaims all 3 rows and the workspace visibly gains hex rows. The A2B diff's run list is a dead Static — only run #0 is ever windowed at ±16 bytes; variant A (master–detail) fixes selection, context and width in one move. The x Operations binding is not fully superseded: the CRC Designer never writes firmware — staged removal recommended.

1 · What the two ghost inputs are — the shipped screen

They are the command bar's #find_input ("Find ASCII text ( / )") and #cmdbar_goto_input ("Goto 0xADDR ( g )"), command_bar.py:139-149. The bar row is height: 3 with a round border (styles.tcss:66-71), leaving one content line — each Input loses its frame and renders as a faint clickable rectangle. They ARE functional: they post the app's Find/Goto messages, and the / and g keys focus exactly these widgets (app.py:5980/5984). Look right of "A2L: (none)":

Baseline — shipped app, 120×34, file loaded. The two dark empty rectangles in the top bar are the ghost inputs. Note the Hex View: 2 data rows visible.
QuestionAnswer
Function?✅ App-wide Find + Goto; landing target of / and g.
Why invisible?3-row bordered bar leaves 1 content line; inputs collapse to dim placeholders.
Deletable?⚠ Yes, with a replacement surface for /·g — variants below.

2 · Command-bar variants — real renders

Variant A — "Summon line": bar deleted, transient input on demand RECOMMENDED

The bar is gone (0 rows). / or g summon a one-row command line docked at the bottom; Enter runs, Esc closes. Compare the Hex View with the baseline: 5 data rows vs 2 — the reclaimed rows are visible, not theoretical. Project/A2L status folds into the Loaded panel.

Variant A, 120×34, summoned state ("/ find: MOT_CAL" at the bottom edge). Idle state is this screen with the bottom line absent.

Variant B — "One-line bar": same widgets, made honest

Same input ids (handlers stay wired), one borderless row with accent key hints; the focused find field shows a real typed value. Reclaims 2 of 3 rows; smallest change.

Variant B, 120×34 — "› proj S19_demo · a2l demo.a2l / [MOT_CAL] g [goto 0xADDR]".

Variant C — "Palette-first": status strip; text entry moves to the palette

One-row status strip, no inputs; /·g open the palette pre-prompted. The capture shows C's cost honestly: the summoned overlay eats ~5 rows and shoves the workspace down.

Variant C, 120×34, palette summoned via "/".
OptionExpected resultConsequences
A — Summon line REC ✅ 3 rows reclaimed everywhere; hex view measurably grows (2→5 rows at 34-row terminal) ⚠ New transient widget + rebind /·g; idle discoverability moves to footer hint + palette
B — One-line bar ✅ 2 rows reclaimed; ghosts become honest fields; near-CSS-only ✅ Lowest risk · ❌ permanent row spent on two rarely-focused inputs
C — Palette-first ✅ 2 rows reclaimed; single text-entry surface ❌ Summoned overlay costs ~5 rows; heaviest refactor; modal hop on the two most common actions

3 · A2B diff — the shipped screen, same fixture

Shipped AbDiffPanel (screens_directionb.py) rendering a real 6-run comparison (engine: diff_mem_maps). Three structural defects, all visible:

Baseline — shipped panel, 132×44. ① run list is a Static: shows 2 of 6 runs, selects nothing — _render_run_windows(0) is the only call, so runs 1..5 are unreachable. ② windows show run #0 at ±16 bytes (DISPLAY_CONTEXT_BYTES) — 3 hex rows in a tall column. ③ three rigid 1fr columns: hex rows wrap unreadably at 1/3 width while vertical space sits empty.

4 · A2B diff variants — real renders, same fixture

Variant A — Master–detail: selectable run list + stacked full-width windows RECOMMENDED

The run list is a real ListView (↑↓ / j/k / click — the selection→window re-render is live in this prototype). Windows stack vertically, take all remaining width, and context is derived from the pane height at render time instead of a constant. The 56-byte changed run is fully highlighted by the real render_hex_view_text highlight path, with the identical "MOT_CAL_" prefix visible in both images.

Variant A, 132×44, run #2 selected. Selection/action rows compacted to one line each (part of the redesign — Input/Button default to 3 rows).

Variant B — Unified interleaved stream

One full-width pane; each run renders as a header + interleaved A/B row pairs with context rows shown once. Every run reachable by scrolling; densest per-row comparison.

Variant B, 132×44 — runs #0-#2 visible; DE AD BE EF vs CA FE BA BE readable line over line.

Variant C — Linked full-height panes + change-map rail

A and B as full-height linked panes over the union address space with a run-colored rail (the memstrip idiom) on the right edge. The capture is the honest verdict: at 132 cols the two 16-byte panes wrap — this layout needs ~190 columns or an 8-byte row mode that render_hex_view_text does not have today.

Variant C, 132×44 — rail renders (amber/cyan marks + viewport arrow), panes wrap.
Measured width ceiling (this box, textual 8.2.8): a full hex+ASCII row is 81 cells. With the 24-col rail: baseline's 3-column layout wraps at any width below ~170; variant A (22-col list + full-width windows) needs ≥ ~130 — clean at 132×44 above, ascii gutter wraps at 120; variant B fits 120 (single pane); variant C needs ~190 or half-width rows. A 120-col fallback for A: drop the run list to an overlay (o key) or shrink it to 12 cols (index+offset only).
OptionExpected resultConsequences
A — Master–detail REC ✅ Fixes selection + context + width in one move; reuses render_hex_view_text (incl. highlight) and the display caps; selection→window path already proven live here ⚠ Static→ListView is a real widget change (focus/keys/tests); needs the 120-col fallback above
B — Unified stream ✅ Densest reading view; fits 120 cols; all runs reachable by scroll ❌ Largest render rewrite; retires the two-image spatial idiom
C — Panes + rail ✅ Best exploration model; rail = existing memstrip idiom ❌ Needs ~190 cols or an 8-byte row mode + windowed rendering; biggest batch

5 · The x Operations binding — premise check first

Operator premise: "the operations binding is unnecessary — CRC calculation is superseded by the CRC Designer."

PropositionVerdictEvidence
The modal's main job is CRC✅ TRUE Registry = crc + two placeholder ops (extract, split_by_segment — no I/O, batch-08).
Designer supersedes the CRC calculation⚠ PARTLY Designer previews/checks and saves *.crc.json templates but never writes firmware bytes (US-V6, crc_designer_view.py:56); its kernel is not yet wired into the crc op (deferred).
Nothing else is lost by deleting the modal❌ FALSE The modal's Write CRC is the only interactive CRC-inject path; Flow Builder covers check+inject only inside a flow with a config file (flow_execution_service.py).
OptionExpected resultConsequences
1 — Remove now ✅ Binding freed, modal + placeholders deleted ⚠ Interactive Write CRC disappears; CRC write becomes Flow-Builder-only — acceptable only by explicit operator ruling
2 — Staged: migrate, then remove REC ✅ Designer gains "Apply to image" (inheriting verify-after-write + dispatch-token guards); follow-up batch deletes modal + x + placeholders ✅ No capability lost, one screen owns CRC end-to-end · ⚠ two batches
3 — Keep as-is❌ Nothing changes ❌ Contradicts intent; duplicate CRC surfaces persist
